verdict: Airbnb's biggest quarter yet: 155 million nights and seats booked drove revenue up 19% to $4.9B, and a lighter tax bill helped net income jump to $1.9B — 39 cents of every revenue dollar.

segments.name: Stays & experiences
segments.note: Service fees charged to hosts and guests on every booking — Airbnb owns almost no property, so its revenue is a cut of each stay. One revenue stream.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Supporting hosts and guests — customer service, trust & safety and host insurance.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Building the app and new products like experiences and services.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing to win travelers and hosts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Bookings accelerated
takeaways.text: Nights and seats booked grew 16% — faster than last quarter — and gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7B as the average daily rate climbed to $179.

takeaways.title: A very profitable model
takeaways.text: Net margin was 39%. Airbnb collects guest money before the stay and owns no hotels, so growth converts unusually cleanly into profit and $1.4B of free cash flow.

takeaways.title: Tax helped the comparison
takeaways.text: Taxes fell to $283M from $418M a year ago, when Airbnb booked a $213M valuation allowance against tax credits — part of why net income grew 38% on 19% revenue growth.

otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$152M: $182M of interest earned (Airbnb holds billions in guest payments before stays happen), minus $45M of interest expense and $15M of other income.
